title: Eval signal mapper and suppression rationale UI for Console alerts
creator: Ravi Shah
description: Problem statement: When an eval-based quality regression fires an alert in Console and is routed to downstream channels (Slack/PagerDuty), engineers and SREs currently get a high-level notification but lack actionable context linking the alert to a specific config or model change. This leads to wasted triage time, repeated noisy alerts, and manual ad-hoc suppressions that are hard to audit.
goals: Surface a deterministic mapping between eval signal delta and the config/model change that likely caused it
Expose the suppression decision rationale in Console (who suppressed, why, duration) and capture it in alert payloads to Slack/PagerDuty
Provide an interactive UI panel on the Evals dashboard that visualizes correlation strength and suggested suppress/auto-ignore windows
Reduce duplicate notifications by implementing a suppression-first dedupe policy that is explainable to oncall and PMs
acceptance_criteria: Console Evals dashboard shows a 'Signal mapping' panel for any regression alert that lists candidate changes (model version, runtime config, quantization profile) with a correlation score
Alert payloads to Slack include the suppression status and a link to the Console rationale view; PagerDuty incidents include minimal suppression metadata and a link back to Console
Operators can create a temporary suppression from the Console panel with prefilled reason templates; actions are recorded in audit logs
Dedupe rules will suppress follow-up notifications when the same root change is implicated and suppression is active; metrics show a >=25% reduction in duplicate pages in the pilot group
Telemetry (dashboard and query) for false-positive suppression reversals is hooked into the Evals Optimize pipeline
design_notes: Figma exploration 1: compact mapping table + sparkline for signal trend (link below)
Design decision: show top 3 candidate changes by correlation score rather than all commits to reduce cognitive load
Accessibility: ensure suppression modal uses concise language and default durations to avoid accidental long suppressions
engineering_considerations: Need a deterministic join between eval sample timestamps and config change events; consider using change-event TTLs to limit candidate window
Correlation algorithm to run in the backend as a cheap heuristic (time-window overlap + effect-size) before scheduling a heavier causality job
Alert payload size constraints for Slack/PagerDuty require a summarized suppression block and Console link; full rationale must live behind the Console URL
Audit trail must be append-only and surfaced in the Console activity feed for compliance
tradeoffs: Aggressive auto-suppression reduces noise but risks hiding real regressions — mitigation: require manual confirmation for auto-suppression above a threshold and expose rollback
More thorough causality analysis is expensive; pragmatic approach is a two-tier pipeline: fast heuristic then async deep analysis
Storing additional change metadata increases retention/costs; we will keep a short TTL for full materialization and index summarized artifacts in the long-term store
decisions: Ship a conservative MVP: show top-3 candidates in Console and allow manual suppress with audit; do not auto-suppress by default
Use heuristic correlation for real-time UX and schedule a background job for full analysis linked in the UI
Include a suppression flag in outbound alert payloads to Slack/PagerDuty and a Console link for complete context

risks: Misattribution: heuristic may surface false candidates leading to incorrect suppressions
User confusion: suppression actions could be used to hide legitimate incidents if UI language is unclear
Operational cost: additional background analysis jobs and retention of change metadata increase infra costs
mitigations: Add friction to create suppression (reason required, default short duration, confirmation modal)
Telemetry to detect suppression->reopen patterns and automatically notify the owner if suppression correlates with missed regressions
Pilot rollout behind feature flag and require explicit opt-in for PagerDuty payload augmentation
